issues.description: The PR publicly enables the heap module while commenting out required allocation APIs and global allocator wiring, leaving downstream heap consumers unable to compile or allocate correctly.
issues.rationale: mm::heap is exported unconditionally, but HeapSlot::alloc_large/dealloc_large, Slab::new/dealloc, the alloc error handler, and the global allocator declaration are all enclosed in block comments. These are executable APIs and wiring used by downstream heap allocator code, not proof-only helpers. Removing them from the public module breaks callers at compile time and disables large/slab allocation paths rather than merely limiting verification. The review reports were AI-assisted, but the fixed final head independently confirms every deletion and the PR remains open without a replacement implementation; the threads being marked resolved does not change the source behavior.
issues.verification: source-only; historical runtime/build not executed. Compared before/after, complete archived and current remote threads, remote final head cb2be5a80af1, downstream API names cited by the reviews, and the still-open PR state.
